messages:
taylor: quick follow-up from the autoscale sync — i'm worried our current drain/evict window will cause a cascade when a tenant spikes. want to brainstorm a predictive-eviction + soft-reservation approach that buys us low-latency for spikes without overcommitting GPUs.

sam: +1. observed two incidents this week where backfill + scale-down overlapped and requests got queued for >3s. headroom math seems brittle.

joni: can you sketch the soft-reservation idea? is it per-tenant token bucket or per-pool credit ledger?

taylor: thinking per-tenant soft tokens (not hard reservations). tokens are a credit balance that can go negative up to a short runway. when negative beyond threshold -> preemptible signal. keeps evictions probabilistic instead of all-or-nothing.

leo: sounds promising. main questions: how do we prevent token-drain attacks (bursty tenants gaming runway)? and how to surface costs?

anya: also want to ensure fairness across SLA tiers. enterprise tenants should have a harder floor on negative balance.

sam: proposal sketch: maintain two counters per tenant: commit_capacity and soft_credit. admission checks first use prefix cache + commit_capacity. if commit_capacity exhausted, allow use of soft_credit up to soft_limit. soft_credit decays (recharges) with a quiet period.

taylor: exact. recharge rate = allocation * alpha, where alpha tuned by tenant SLA. and we add a cooldown hysteresis window after a scale-down to avoid immediate re-use.

leo: pseudo config snippet:
```
tenant: acme
commit_capacity: 8
soft_limit: 16
recharge_rate_per_min: 2
negative_runway_ms: 5000
cooldown_after_scale_down_ms: 60000
```

joni: question: eviction policy when pool low on GPUs and many tenants negative — random drop vs priority queue? we need predictable SLOs.

taylor: priority queue by SLA + recent success rate. but to avoid starvation, we also apply capped fairness: any tenant with >X failures gets bump in priority.

sam: another concern: state churn. tracking per-request token ops at high QPS might spike control-plane DB ops. we should approximate with local caches + periodic reconciliation, not sync-per-request.

anya: agree. local ephemeral counters on the operator with a write-behind to the ledger. if operator dies, reconciliation reconciles to global ledger.

leo: what about predictive eviction using short-term signal from request rate derivative? e.g., if rate increases > R over T, prewarm an ephemeral headroom by borrowing from low-util tenants for Y seconds. helps cold-starts.

taylor: nice. combine derivative-based prewarm + soft tokens. derivative triggers ephemeral burst lane that can be clawed back if overall pressure persists.

joni: operational hooks: need metrics for soft_credit_balance, negative_runway_count, ephemeral_burst_active, reclaimed_from_tenant. also alerts when reconciliation lag > threshold.

sam: rollout plan idea: feature-flag per-cluster, start with small tenants pool, observe reclaimed counts and tail latency. toggles: enable-predictive-prewarm, enable-soft-tokens, enable-clawback.

taylor: Agree. action items: leo to prototype local token cache + reconciliation sketch; joni to draft eviction priority queue rules and fairness cap; sam to run smallscale sim with synthetic spikes; anya to map SLA rentention to soft_limit/recharge. i'll schedule a 30m design check next week.

devops-bot: meeting created: #design-check 02/12 09:30 — invites sent to taylor, sam, joni, leo, anya. :calendar:

taylor: thanks everyone. keep replies short here if you discover blockers, otherwise we'll review prototypes in the meeting. :thumbsup:
